summary: Retires the TLV mechanism in the Associated Channel Header of the MPLS Generic Associated Channel. No channel type uses ACH TLVs, and handling them in hardware causes problems on the fast path, so this document updates RFC 5586 to remove them.

plainLanguage.summary: A mail form had an extra box nobody ever filled in, and it slowed the clerks down. So they crossed it off.

questions: what does rfc 7026 remove from rfc 5586
what is the mpls generic associated channel
subtitle: MPLS drops the never-used TLV option from the Associated Channel Header and deletes its IANA registry.

tldr.problem: RFC 5586 let the MPLS Generic Associated Channel carry ACH TLVs, but none of the 18 defined channel types allows them and TLVs are hard to process in hardware.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC deletes Section 3 of RFC 5586, states that a G-ACh message MUST NOT be preceded by an ACH TLV, and removes the related IANA registry and column.
tldr.outcome: ACH TLVs are retired. It updates RFC 5586.

today: RFC 7026 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5586. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: ACH TLVs and Why They Go
sections.content:
RFC 4385 says that if the first nibble of a pseudowire packet over MPLS is 1, the packet starts with the Associated Channel Header (ACH). That creates a message channel tied to one pseudowire. RFC 5586 generalized it into the MPLS Generic Associated Channel (G-ACh) for MPLS Sections, LSPs and pseudowires, and defined optional ACH TLVs that add context.

At the time of writing, none of the 18 defined ACH Channel Types allows ACH TLVs, and there were no unexpired Internet-Drafts that use them. G-ACh packets are meant to be processed substantially in hardware, and TLVs bring unpredictable formats and lengths that make that difficult. The RFC calls them not useful and possibly harmful.
sections.plainLanguage: Nobody used the optional extra box, and its odd sizes made the machines slower. So it had to go.

sections.title: What Changes in RFC 5586
sections.content:
Section 3 of RFC 5586 is deleted. References to ACH TLVs in Section 4 of that RFC should be disregarded, because with Section 3 gone no TLVs will be present.

The implication for the ACH is stated flatly: a G-ACh message MUST NOT be preceded by an ACH TLV. The RFC makes no comment about TLVs in other places, and proposals to use TLVs within or appended to ACH messages are out of scope.
sections.plainLanguage: The rule book page about the extra box is torn out, and a new rule says the box must never be used.

sections.title: IANA Registry Changes
sections.content:
IANA deleted the "Associated Channel Header TLV Registry", a subregistry of "Pseudowire Name Spaces (PWE3)", and left a tombstone record marked DELETED that references RFC 5586 and this document.

IANA also deleted the "TLV Follows" column from the "Pseudowire Associated Channel Types" registry, leaving no record.
sections.plainLanguage: The list of extra boxes was thrown away, with a note saying it used to exist. A column in another list was erased completely.

sections.title: Manageability and Security
sections.content:
The RFC says removal has no impact on manageability because no ACH types allow TLVs. Packet sniffers that look for ACH TLVs are not harmed by the deletion.

Removal has a marginal positive effect on security because the feature might have been used to carry false information or to bloat G-ACh messages. No mechanism had been proposed for using TLVs to carry security parameters. The RFC treats security as the job of whichever specification defines a G-ACh message.
sections.plainLanguage: Taking away the unused box makes it a little harder to sneak something nasty into the mail.

references.text: Bryant, S., Swallow, G., Martini, L., and D. McPherson, "Pseudowire Emulation Edge-to-Edge (PWE3) Control Word for Use over an MPLS PSN", RFC 4385, February 2006.
Bocci, M., Ed., Vigoureux, M., Ed., and S. Bryant, Ed., "MPLS Generic Associated Channel", RFC 5586, June 2009.
